prompt:
Create ONE polished enemy selection concept sheet for a first-person music-fantasy survival roguelite. Match the attached reference sheet's exact visual language and presentation: landscape 16:9, a clean FOUR COLUMNS by TWO ROWS grid, pale warm ivory background, thin warm gold grid dividers, eight complete full-body character concepts, generous separation, soft grounding shadows. This is a NEW roster: DO NOT copy characters or old numbers from reference. Each cell contains exactly ONE distinct character and a large dark burgundy two-digit number beneath it. No other text. Equal visual importance, no overlapping bodies, no cropped feet, props or head ornaments. Characters may be scaled within their cells for readability, not a physical scale chart.
STYLE: retro hand-painted Japanese animation translated to refined 3D cel-shaded game concept art, crisp ink contours, expressive silhouettes, decisive two/three-tone hard shadows, matte painted wood and cloth, antique brass, ivory, burgundy, midnight indigo, restrained muted teal. Charming but clearly hostile music-fantasy creatures. Not photorealistic, not chibi, not generic steampunk robots. Music theme beyond theater: enchanted acoustic instruments, rhythm beasts, resonance spirits, musical symbols. Keep anatomy buildable, detailed enough to model but not noisy. No guns, sci-fi equipment, neon equalizers, gore, stage scenery, HUD, ability labels, attacks or effects covering character anatomy. Do not give every character the same porcelain face mask; use species-specific faces and expressions.
EXACT NUMBER LAYOUT: top row 25, 26, 27, 28; bottom row 29, 30, 31, 32. Only these eight number labels.
25 TREBLE-CLEF WYRM: small serpentine flying dragon, body and curling neck trace a clearly readable golden treble-clef silhouette, two translucent indigo fins, expressive narrow ivory face, trailing burgundy ribbon tail. Organic magical creature, no instrument robot.
26 STAFF-WEAVER SPIDER: eight-legged ink-blue spider with a circular ivory abdomen marked by five clean musical staff lines, delicate brass joint accents and burgundy bowlike crest, five close parallel silken threads loop between two front feet only. Clearly spider, no full background web.
27 REST-SIGN SHADE: a sharp angular floating dark-violet shadow creature whose whole silhouette resembles a quarter-rest musical sign, one narrow ivory eye slit, two tapered ribbon arms and zigzag descending tail, gold edging. Minimal iconic shape, no sheet-paper body.
28 CHOIR LANTERN SPIRIT: floating ornate ivory-and-gold lantern with three small different expressive porcelain singing faces around its central chamber, softly glowing warm core, burgundy tassels and small crown-like roof. Distinct hovering architectural silhouette, no bell dome.
29 WANDERING CONDUCTOR: slender adult masked fantasy conductor with charcoal tailcoat, burgundy lining, ivory gloves, asymmetric feathered hat, one thin wooden baton and the other expressive open hand; no instrument body, no metronome torso. Strong readable commanding posture, full boots visible.
30 VINYL REAPER: lean humanoid raven-headed figure in folded midnight-blue cloak, huge black vinyl record tilted behind shoulders like a circular mantle, concentric grooves and ivory center label, one curved tonearm staff held low. Analog enchanted music aesthetic, no futuristic tech, no gore.
31 WIND-CHIME WILLOW: small walking willow spirit with elegant dark wooden trunk, long hanging pale gold tubular chimes mixed with burgundy ribbon leaves, root feet, tiny ivory eyes in bark. Cascading vertical silhouette, actual chimes readable, no large environment tree.
32 RESONANT CRYSTAL COLOSSUS: imposing nonhumanoid heavy stone-and-crystal guardian with broad shoulders, pale ivory faceted acoustic-quartz chest cavity, clearly exposed graduated glass-harmonica bowls floating in a close vertical stack inside the cavity, chunky dark indigo forearms and feet, subtle teal resonance light. No guns, circuitry or helmets; magical musical resonance anatomy.
Match reference palette and rendering closely, while all eight silhouettes must be distinct and new.
